commit.message:
Fix Xom UC + Cleaving+C crashes (Oneirical)

The call in attacks to handle concussion brand presumes the only way to
access concussion brand would be via having a weapon (so it can check
if it's Carina At Dusk). This is no longer the case as of 7a79339, where
even unarmed characters may be granted the brand as part of Xom's
Cleaving+? blessing effect; this fixes the crash by checking if the player
has a weapon before investigating that weapon.

Fix Yara's not exploding properly

Rather than its normal damaging blast, it was simply removing status
effects from monsters in range instead. (Was broken by 809370f1d4)

This fixes #5560

Fix a crash using elemental colours for flash_tile() in console/webtiles

This fixes #5562
Fix a typo
Add changelog entry.

Changelog update through 9be42e2

While we're never going to be too precise about how Xom precisely works in
this abbreviated document format, Their changes are so involved that it's
good to get out a prompt and lengthy changelog description for Their
rework this version.

Don't auto-recall jade crystals or Xom guardians onto traps

(Or poltergeist haunted armour, for that matter.)

Update Xom's in-game description

To remove mentions of mood, and add mentions of chaos blessings.

(I sort of wanted to fit in a note about the chaos blessings rotating, but
it felt hard to shoehorn it into this format.)

Display on the player's tile when they're confused

Since it can happen unexpected with Xom and sometimes isn't obvious until
you've stumbled away from something already.
Make inwards ring animations actually reach radius 0

Decouple Xom's action chance from player action speed

Xom's roll to do something happened at a fixed chance every turn. This
meant that if a player was attacking with a fast weapon, Xom would act much
more often than if they were using a slow one (or in statue form, running
away).

Instead, multiply the action chance by how long the turn took so that Xom
will act at closer to a constant rate no matter how fast or slow you are.
(This does make Xom actions more consistent if you're *very* slow, but if
that's true, you probably need all the help you can get.)

Since 'attacking faster than 10 aut' is something Xom characters typically
spend a lot of time doing, this will result in a general reduction in Xom's
action rate in normal combat. But c6feab1a7 will likely also result in the
player having higher tension when in a variety of bad situations, which
should counterbalance this somewhat. (Also: it's a flat benefit when slowed
or some other bad situations).

Slightly rescale Xom tension bar and tension-based action chance

Instead of Xom's chance of acting capping at 4* on the piety bar, stretch
it out to cap at 6*. (This chance is very slightly higher than old 4* was,
but requires a fair bit more tension to hit that chance.)

Also, linearly interpolate between pips instead of each one representing a
hard breakpoint on Xom's attention. (And very slightly reduce Xom's chance
of negative actions at high tension.)

Finally, move the breakpoints down by one (except the bottom one), for
reasons of aesthetics. (So that 3* starts at 10 instead of 11, etc.)

Make Xom better at telling if a monster can smite you (regret-index)

Xom's plant ring is supposed to be a more-positive-than-negative effect,
and specifically avoids using it if there are too many monsters still able
to damage you from the other side of the plants.

This was done by _mons_has_smite_attack(), which uses a curated (and very
incomplete) list of such things. Instead, use threat_range() which should
be more exhaustive about what attacks are capable of threatening the player
without line of fire.

_mons_has_smite_attack() in general is a bit dubious, but the other caller
of it at the moment is determining whether a monster will attempt to swap
with other monsters to approach the player (if _mons_has_smite_attack() is
true, they will not). Making more such monsters remain at the back of
fights to make the player's life difficult sounds good in general, but I
am reluctant to make such a diffuse change this close to feature freeze in
case there are undesireable side-effects or exceptions that need to be
carved out. For next version, perhaps.

Move Xom's single ally summon from a 0-tension effect to an explore effect

To slightly pad out some of the lower value effects

Yet further tension calculation updates

As with previous tension commits, this both intends to make tension a more
accurate tool for potential usage beyond Xom / Beogh challenges / the
Singing Sword, but also to reflect tension finally being visible to
players after e60639e.

 * The effects of one's current HP provide a nonlinear multiplier on
   one's current tension values, which is reasonable in theory (most
   characters regularly dip to 80% HP in a fight) and fairly painfully
   low with current numbers in practice unless one is at the very edge of
   death (and even before then, being at 50% HP means the fight is a lot
   more than just 33% more dangerous). This formula has been adjusted to
   scale reasonably more to make it judge situations better while
   preserving its nonlinear arrangement, the end results of which are
   demonstrated in this chart:

   HP% | 100%|  90%|  80%|  70%|  60%|  50%|  40%|  30%|  20%|  10%|   1%|
   -----------------------------------------------------------------------
   Old | 1.00| 1.05| 1.11| 1.18| 1.25| 1.33| 1.43| 1.54| 1.67| 1.82| 1.98|
   New | 1.00| 1.07| 1.15| 1.25| 1.36| 1.50| 1.67| 1.88| 2.14| 2.50| 2.94|

 * The severity of how much the player is poisoned now also factors into
   said HP assesment, with one's effective health being reduced by a third
   of such poison- while it can be quickly cured, many fights with lower
   poison amounts don't warrant such, and thus it still has some direct
   impact on one's HP and actions as it ticks down.

 * Badform transformations and low MP now count for higher tension
   multipliers. The latter's condition is now a bit more complicated-
   rather than just checking is at 10% or less MP, it checks if one
   is at 25% or less MP and doesn't apply to Trog worshippers without
   any spirit shield. (While this doesn't really carefully check over
   players lacking spells or invocations that don't cost MP, the
   majority of notable MP drain effects like having activated mp-draining
   traps or fighting ghost moths are fairly dangerous anyway).

 * New status effects tracked on monsters now include Touch of Paradox,
   Phase Shift, and being Dazed. New conditions tracked for players
   include being in the Crucible of Flesh or Okawaru's Arena, with the
   former also having nonzero minimum tension in the same fashion as
   the Abyss or the orb run.

 * A little bit more clean-up and reorganizing has been done here, most
   notably removing player Vex after it got folded into cannot_act in
   d46125b.

Veto Xom hostile summon while the player is at very low health

And generally reduce its weight in the zero-tension list. (With more
effects moved out of it, it became very common.)

Make Xom fake shatter usable out of combat

Fake shatter wasn't on the zero-tension list because of concerns that its
ability to (sometimes, poorly, loudly) dig into vaults could cause players
to sit around for long periods of time, waiting for it to happen.

As a solution to that, it can only destroy hard walls while at non-zero
tension (but can sometimes happen without it, making noise and messing up
the local terrain).

New negative Xom effect: Make traps (regret-index)

This is a non-exploration zero-tension effect that places 3-9 random traps
in sight of the player. They mostly obey the branch and depth restrictions
normal generation uses (ie: won't place Zot traps in early game), but won't
place teleport or shaft traps, and may always place net or harlequin traps.

These traps should never be placed in ways that locally disconnect the
terrain (so you'll never be forced to step on one).

Intended to slightly broaden the pool of negative non-explore effects.

Move Xom doom out of the explore pool and into the zero-tension pool

This effect doesn't tend to do much. The doom it applies is small, and
there is additional downscaling if the player is heavily doomed already,
making it unlikely to ever result in a meaningful penalty unless the player
has a lot of doom from an outside source.

It was intended to 'pad out' more impactful negative explore effects, but
in general, playtesting has led to me to conclude that many of those
effects aren't quite common enough.

As policy, most long-term negative effects shouldn't be in the non-explore
pool to avoid penalizing resting/backtracking, but since this one *in
practice* doesn't usually cause real problems, I am moving it there to
round out the fact that there are so few non-combat negative effects left
on the non-explore list.

Adjust logic for Xom good mutation gifts

The downweighting done in 41e759f to reduce Xom's likelihood of giving good
mutations, the more mutated the player already is, was done backwards,
resulting vastly fewer positive mutations being given in general (with a 0%
chance unless the player was already mutated somehow).

But even if this logic was turned around, good mutations becoming less
likely as the player gets more mutated (but *bad* mutations never becoming
less likely) seems like it would have the net effect of the player slowly
growing worse over time in some cases.

Instead, reduce the odds of a good mutation based only on how many *good*
mutations the player already has, and give a chance for a good mutation to
instead remove a bad mutation directly.

Adjust Xom's summon / guardian pool

With Xom's summons pool gaining new power pressure from the new guardian
blessing and less design pressure with all of the other new hostile Xom
strategic effects this batch, Xom's summon pool can do with some
notable adjustments.

This commit gets to a fair number of belated individual monster
adjustments in Xom's list: drudes were incorrectly given the old quasit
level range back in 5a39f0a, neqoxecs shouldn't appear for as long
post-0e930c6, sin beasts never got the bands from b0d9199, and ynoxinuls
should be a bit higher post 6c75973. Aside from this, there's a general
effort to weaken the very lowest level summons (when players have very
few tools and it's the most pressured to optimize fleeing potential
every rest) and somewhat notably buff summons between XLs 15 to 21 (as
many players have fairly settled offenses after the first Lair branch,
most hostile summons were being extended past their reasonable lifespan to
die in a few quick swings or spells). This also works out for guardians,
where the presence of a reviving ally is strongest early, and to keep help
making sure Xom blessings still are tangibly strong and thus noticed even
once one has their own settled offense.

This commit does mean there's a bit less variety at any given point,
though there's a fair bit of level randomization per pull as is (which
should probably do with more assessment post-severity-removal). With
bits and pieces of extended update monsters having been worked on but
not pushed during 0.35, there should be plenty more to work with after
such is returned to during the 0.36 dev cycle. In the interim, there's
enough additional negative Xom effects in this commit batch that it should
be fine alongside the rest of this sprawling major update.

New bad Xom explore effect: Hall of Mirrors

This creates 5-10 indistinguishable clones of a monster and encircles the
player with them (at a small distance), except that all but the original
have vastly reduced HP (-70%) and inflict greatly reduced damage against
the player (-80%) and cast spells at 1/3rd the normal rate.

More scary than truly dangerous in *most* cases, but non-damaging things
these monsters can do can sometimes add up in a real big way. They're very
vulnerable to AoE, so should be managable in most cases in a number of ways
but hopefully plenty dramatic.

(The maybe-fake status icon was made by regret-index.)

Don't hide certain statuses which change the player's tile when in a form

Being transformed would prevent the player from visibly changing during the
Executioner or Disguised status or when the Partisan of Prune was active.

Now these should instead override form tiles temporarily.

Remove a case of phantom Fear persisting invisibly on monsters (Roxie)

If a monster was afraid and ran into a dead end, and decided to stop
fleeing on account of this while out of sight of its foe (usually the
player), it would stop fleeing but not lose ENCH_FEAR.

This was often invisible, but it meant that:
a) They could be targeted by Bestial Takedown for no obvious reason
b) They would remain immune to further Fear until the status wore off - a
   fact which even the targeter UI would not indicate.

This bug has likely existed forever, but was just very hard to notice
happening in most circumstances (very easy to assume the monster just made
its will check rather than being inexplicably immune to fear).

Simplify/standardize block/reflection messages

Message composition for reflected projectiles was phrased in approximately
6 different ways, depending on whether the blocker was a player or monster,
the projectile was an attack or a beam, and whether a shield of reflection
was used or some other source.

This unifies all types of blocks to use standard phrasing and shortens the
message in many cases. Most non-shield sources no longer say that the
attack was blocked 'by an invisible shield', and reflection messages no
longer print the shield's full name. You just get "X blocks Y ...and
reflects it back!"

With an exception that when divine shield blocks either a projectile *or*
a melee attack, it is now listed first. (ie: "Your divine shield blocks the
juggerenaut's attack."). It feels appropriate to me that which blocks are
eating up this effect stand out a little.

Don't state twice that the player is blinded by attacking a divine shield

It's currently very hard for the player to attack something with a divine
shield, but odds are good it will become a lot easier at some point in the
future.

Remove some superfluous code to handle naming unseen monsters

Several places manually checked whether a monster was visible to decide
whether to print its name or "something". But monster::name() already
returns "something" for unseen monsters on its own, making this
superfluous.

The attack classes had a particularly extensive implementation of this,
which (as far as I can tell) isn't doing anything that monster::name()
wouldn't. (It was first added in 0e5f00f when this was not true, but ported
to the current attack class structure in 2010731, at which point I believe
it may have already been redundant?)

Hopefully, this commit results in no functional change.

Don't crash when sensing an invisible hydra

It's currently hard to encounter an invisible hydra, but if one *did*, the
game would assert the moment the player sensed them, since it would usually
think they had 0 heads (which asserts).

Instead, don't comment on how many heads invisible hydra have at all (which
is consistent with hiding most other 'status effects') and use an
approximately average number for their tiles.

Remove Xom's chance to give a stealth bonus (or noise) on a new floor (r-i)

The former is handled more interestingly now by the blessing of disguise,
which makes this feel a bit vestigial to me.

Xom blessing: Sneaky

This blessing makes the player a master of disguise and trickery, giving
them short blade-tier stabbing on any weapon and causing them to
automatically conceal themselves as a bush or barrel or similar nondescript
object when they are first spotted by enemies.

While disguised, the player cannot be noticed by anything, no matter what,
and they also have a 100% chance of succeeding on distraction stabs.
Attacking, casting a spell, using an ability, reading a scroll, or evoking
an item will instantly break the effect (drinking potions is okay). It will
also expire after a short length of time.

When the effect breaks, the player will be unable to disguise themselves
again for a short exploration-based cooldown *unless* there are both no
hostile monsters currently in sight *and* all monsters which were in sight
when the disguise was first donned are dead. (Leave no witnesses!)

(On a practical level, it means that if the automatic disguise is triggered
by a relatively harmless monster, you can just stab it without feeling
frustrated that the cooldown was wasted, but it additionally sometimes
results in a cute minigame of trying to maneuver to hide yourself from a
a single additional witness while trying to stab someone else, further
aiding the stealth sim allusion baked into this blessing.)

I very much look forward to hearing about someone walking off with the Orb
as a bush.

(For the record, I would have also let you hide in a cardboard box if they
weren't too modern an invention for Crawl.)

--------------------

The disguise tiles were made by regret-index, combining Sastreii's
occultist with old Frogatto leaf assets by Guido Bos and Jetrel released
as CC0, CC0 barrels made by Hyptosis and edited by AntumDeluge, CC0 JRPG
rocks made by finalbossblues, and ontoclasm's various granite statue
tiles.

Xom blessing: Protean

This blessing causes aspiring flesh to burst from the player's body when
they fall below 70% HP. These transform into monsters more slowly than
those from a protean progenitor and the monsters they spawn only last a
short while.

The HD of monsters generated depends on the player's XL, and there is a
medium-length cooldown after each time it happens.

Add a line-break between shield's item and penalty descriptions.

A little more readable not to be in the same block (especially for unrand
shields).

Allow the Warlock's Mirror to reflect explosive projectiles

Such as fireballs.

I suspect them not working was largely for technical reasons (since it's
impossible, code-wise, to reflect them at the point where reflection is
normally checked). This mild refactoring instead allows reflecting them
*before* the explosive projectile turns into an explosion. (You still can't
block an actual explosion you're engulfed in.)

The standard chance to omnireflect something that isn't dodgeable seemed
rather high for this effect, so I have set it to 2/5ths of that amount and
updated the description accordingly.

Xom Blessing: Chaos Battleshape (regret-index)

This provides a battlesphere-like companion that appears whenever the
player is in combat and rapidly respawns when destroyed.

It triggers when the player performs a melee attack, firing a chaos
projectile at a random enemy (with a tiny chance of applying a debuff). But
each shot it fires also causes it to gain charge and transform. When it
reaches its final stage (a battledodecahedron), it stops firing melee bolts
and can instead be detonated by casting any spell.

The level of the spell causes one of the 3 sets of effects:
Level 1-4: Does smite-targeted chaos damage to 3 random enemies (with a 25%
           chance of a chaos effect)
Level 5-7: Targets 5 enemies instead and the battleshape splits apart into
           a bunch of shooting stars.
Level 8-9: Targets 7 enemies instead and does a 3x3 explosions of damage
           instead of single target (ie: a little like Ignition) and
           creates even more shooting stars.

Triggering the strongest effects from this will probably be somewhat rare
for many Xom worshippers (especially those comfortable with engaging in a
bunch of melee before casting them), but it provides a powerful incentive
to train higher level spells and build a more hybrid character.

And, worst come to worst, it's a solid amount of extra damage output in
most fights and the chance for a useful debuff.

-------------------

The battleshape tiles were made by regret-index, using CC0 polyhedra models
made by LucasBrown, TilmannR, and Tomruen.

Don't forget that a beam was BEAM_CHAOS when reusing it

It would otherwise 'lock in' whatever flavour was last rolled for it.

Fix a few duplicate/buggy vfx draws

When c106424 made it so that projectiles still draw themselves on the tile
they hit, there were a number of cases when things that had been *intended*
to be invisible now rendered. In a few of these cases, the projectile
graphic did not even look like the intended appearance of the effect,
resulting in some ugly double-drawing (eg: for Fulsome Fusillade and
Shadow Tempest).

In some cases, flash_tile() had been used as a surrogate for the regular
bolt projectile draw, and is now removed. In others, flash_tile()
represents more correct timings, and the beam was set to not animate
instead.
Fix spacing

Xom blessing: Mannequin Troupe (regret-index)

Styled passingly after Yred's reaping aura and Dith's marionette, this
blessing causes Xom to gift the player mannequins of monsters the player
killed themselves, after each battle is complete.

Mannequins are a new form of dervived (nonliving) monster. They are frailer
and weaker than zombies (and lack any resists beyond the standard nonliving
package), but retain all their spells and wield standard equipment for a
monster of their base type. They cannot be made from uniques or
insubstantial monsters, but otherwise can cosplay even undead or other
nonliving monsters (even stationary ones).

Their attacks and spells are much weaker than the base monster, and most
non-movement actions slightly damage them (giving them a limited shelf-life
in combat), though their cast rate is significantly increased (in part, to
avoid wasting those actions on less impactful things). In addition, if they
had only close range attacks, they gain the Blink Close spell. Otherwise
they gain the Blink Range spell and the cautious flag.

A passive that continually creates mannequins out of things you fight has
a somewhat similar dynamic to Yred, but only getting them at the *end* of
combat (defined here by 'after 7 consecutive turns with no enemies in LoS)
changes the dynamic fairly considerably - creating a sort of ebb and flow
where your prior army gets slowly ground down, and then replaced in a big
burst once a large battle is complete. (It can also make fights at the
entrance to a branch considerably more pressured, but with a big reward
afterward.)

Requiring the player to score the kills themselves hopefully creates a
natural rubber-banding on army size (ie: the more mannequins you get, the
smaller percentage of kills will be by your own hands, meaning fewer new
mannequins), and mannequins refuse to acknowledge player commands,
hopefully preventing the tedious play of trying to make them *not*
kill-steal from you: the only way to do this ought to be to rush into the
fray after them!

-----------------------

Don't hide weapons of most stationary monsters

This wasn't currently consequential since an exception was specifically
carved out for training dummies (which are the only stationary monster we
currently use that *has* weapons), however the code for 'displaying an item
beneath a monster' and 'displaying a monster's weapon and shield' were
mutually exclusive for as far as I can tell, no good reason (dating all the
way back to 151a128 )

It effectively also prevented marking items under training dummies, too.
Improve the 'foot' names for player djinni and poltergeist

Xom blessing: Spellstride

This gives the player Rampage and makes it so that whenever they rampage
towards a foe, they spawn a living spell in their trail for each step they
take (at the cost of 1 MP each).

These living spells can cast either quicksilver bolt, corrosive bolt, bolt
of light, bolt of flesh, bolt of devastation, or bolt of antimagic. Which
spell is determined when the blessing is given and will remain the same for
all living spells created during its entire duration.

Their damage scales with XL (and is kept artificially low at low XL via a
rather hacky forced override for living spells, but otherwise there was
simply no way to lower the damage sufficiently on many of them - even HD 1
corrosive bolt is 3d8.)

It's useless-to-actively-detrimental in corridors, but potentially very
strong in many other situations, allowing the player to build up these
living spells behind themselves and sidestep to unleash on enemies in a
burst. And different builds may have different ways to exploit some of
their side-effects as well.

-------------------

New living spell pallette swap tiles were made by regret-index, using the
default living spell tile by CanOfWorms.

Make living spells peripheral

So, among other things, Xom won't attempt to buff them.
Allow allies to shoot through living spells

Make living spells dissipate if the player swaps with them

In mostly the same way that foxfires do already.

Monsters will instead refuse to swap with them, which I suspect is *mostly*
a behavioural improvement (since you'd rather the spell be in front of the
stone giant, where it can fire itself, instead of trapped behind where it
will probably expire instead).

This change is intended largely to make an upcoming Xom effect play a bit
more interestingly, but player access to living spells is presently almost
entirely via Xom already, so it should have limited balance effect.

Xom blessing: Guardians

Riffing off Hep ancestors, this blessing has Xom grant you a long-term
respawning companion (or sometimes several at once, depending on the type
of guardian granted).

Like ancestors, the player is able to freely fire through them, and they
will automatically respawn after a moderate delay, each time they are
killed. (Though if they die a great many times, they will respawn greatly
weakened for the remaining duration of the blessing.)

Since this draws from Xom's normal summon list, there is a large variety of
monsters that can become your guardian (based on the player's XL), which
should give a fair bit of *internal* variation to this one blessing as
well.

Xom blessing: Chaos Eisegesis (regret-index)

Riffing off Sif Muna's Repeat Exegesis ability, this Xom blessing grants
the player chaotic knowledge of a random spell (chosen from a curated list,
with spell level influenced by your XL). While the blessing lasts, the
player may cast this spell using the Chaos Eisegesis ability, with power
based purely on their XL (ignoring spell skills entirely) and with magic
contamination as its only cost. This amount of contam is fairly high and
increases based on a factor of the spell's level and your current XL.

This tends to mean that anything is free to use once or twice per battle
(and often more, if the spell level is a little low for your XL), but you
can be pushing your luck to use it as freely as you might want. Though if
the player feels like gambling with contam and pushing their limits
sometimes, Xom will be happy about that, too.

For the most part, I have deliberately excluded summons from the spell list
(since multiple other blessings and Xom effects involve allies) unless they
are somewhat unusual or not something that really works when given
passively by Xom (such as Surprising Crocodile or Monarch Bomb).

(This commit also adds a little to the basic blessing framework, now that
there is more than one implemented blessing to cycle between.)

Turn Xom's cleaving status into a blessing, with extra bonuses

As a blessing, it is permanent until Xom cycles your blessing out for
something else. In addition to granting cleaving, it now also makes the
player's weapon act as if it was additionally branded with either
sundering, concussion, valour, entangling, or rebuke, no matter its weapon
type: even your hands! (The given brand is chosen when the blessing is
handed out and remains the same until it ends.)

Finally, the player is given a flat +5 slaying, to help it feel more
relevant in the early game, when the player is less likely to be able to
safely exploit the cleaving itself.

Note: when this blessing gives entangling, the player becomes capable of
entangling unlimited things at once with it, too!

(I left devious off the brand list since many players won't be able to
consistently activate its effect at all, and a later blessing will aid
stealth play more directly.)

Add basic framework for Xom blessings

This is intended as a major new system for Xom, providing obvious player
power though a means more reliable than 'randomly chooses to win a fight
for you' or the narrow chance of a good acquirement, while still hopefully
feeling adequately chaotic and Xom-like.

These will be a series of powerful passives, *one* of which will always be
active at any given time, but which one it *is* will rotate over time,
after some large-ish amount of kills/XP. These are intended to cycle often
enough that you never rely on keeping the power you want, but last long
enough that you can at least get used to having and using a certain one
for a while before it is snatched away.

On a philosophy level, this is leaning into the idea that Xom shouldn't
*just* be a 'challenge god', where people debate whether or not they're
better than having no god at all. But a god whose power is obviously
positive, but unpredictable (and which will still *try* to kill you
periodically). Some of these blessings will probably be quite strong, but I
think the random nature of Xom's negative effects means that they will
safely never be a dominating god choice, and the hope is that this makes
them feel more fun and engaging (and rewarding) to a wider variety of
players.

Change default shortcut for scroll of butterflies

It caused issues when both appeared in the same run (as is possible with
multiple backgrounds).

Make hostile Xom teleport less common

It can no longer happen at 0 tension, outside of exploration
effects (reducing incentive to rest on a different floor), and
generally making one of the worst exploration effects in general
less frequent.

Fix Xom's sticky fireballs not checking rF for its direct damage

And instead using res_sticky_flame() (ie: whether or not the monster is
insubstantial, currently).

Allow Xom wrath to pick explore actions

Which tend to be the most appropriate for random wrath effects anyway.

Change some polymorph behaviour

Monsters chosen for a monster's polymorph set were forced to always share
all habitat types of the original monster (ie: a flying monster could only
polymorph into other flying monsters). This makes sense for generating a
predetermined list that will never cause the wand to fail over any terrain.

However, this resulted in a couple of issues for non-wand-based polymorphs:
 -Chaos weapon polymorph was often wildly deadly early in the game, since
  while bats are harmless, almost every other flying monster in the game is
  much deadlier, commonly pulling steam dragons or even killer bees on D:1
 -Polymorph effects intended to make a monster more or less dangerous (eg:
  Xom or the Degeneration card) did no habit check of any sort, meaning
  they could often fail over deep water / lava.

Now, most non-wand-based sources do a habitability check for the monster's
*current* terrain. This makes early chaos brand less of a trap to use on
some monsters and makes a few god effects fail less often.

This commit also fixes an issue where wands of polymorph would always fail
to do anything to a shapeshifter not on land (since it would first revert
them to their original form, which can't swim). This feels superfluous to
me, since they instantly change back to another monster anyway, so instead
just turn them into a random monster.

Also, don't prevent shapeshifters from changing shape while taking stairs.
(The reasoning for this one appears to be ancient and involved players
being confused by permanent allies being polymorphed during stair transit.
I don't think this is a relevant issue.)

Give Chaos Knights a scroll of summoning

While their armour and weapon are pretty good, they have a greater than

while now.)

Starting with two mutually-exclusive items is also cutely Xom-flavoured in
a minor way (and ?summoning, while powerful, is innately unpredictable).

Which are all pretty useful, actually! Just less commonly less useful than

(I think there's room for even more of these items to be made in future,

Short of exceptional circumstances, these items should not be placed

New positive Xom explore effect: Random knowledge (regret-index)

Intended as an !experience-like effect, except outside the player's
control. This very rare effect provides the player with a large amount of
skill in 3 different skills that are heavily weighted to not be among those
the player is already significantly invested in (or any skills which would
cross-train with those).

In other words, it gives quite a lot of XP but usually in places where the

New negative Xom effect: Stair lock

This locks all stairs on the floor until the player kills a certain
small-ish number of monsters.

It uses reachability checks to ensure that at least these many monsters
exist somewhere the player can walk to without the use of consumables and
if the player somehow manages to leave the floor anyway (such as via
banishment), they will unlock automatically.

There is a small possibility that this might happen on a disconnected floor
and Xom could teleport the player to the other side of it when they lack
any ?tele of their own, 'trapping' them there. But I think the odds of this
are quite low and Xom will *eventually* teleport you out again anyway, so
hopefully it's fine.

(I expect this to be a relatively low-impact event in a lot of cases, but
we need some of those to round out the possibility space and this should
hopefully be scary in an interesting way some of the time.)

Unlike many similar effects, it also has a small chance to happen as a
non-explore effect, in part due to the helpful property that it can almost
never punish shopping trips since it can only trigger on floors with a
bunch of reachable monsters still alive on them.

Add non-placeholder layouts + new tiles for Xom's Arena

For the most part, these maps loosely echo Okawaru's Duel arenas but made
slightly larger, with appropriately-Xom flavoured decorations and
spectators. They have no wall or floor randomization, to match said
Duel arenas, but otherwise still contain a bunch of other effects.

 * Gimmicks can appear at XL 4+ and can be any of a 5% chance of
   seething chaos generators (close to the player's start but never
   on the starting arch), a 2.5% chance of traps (harlequin and
   dispersal by default, with a further small chance of Zot traps
   after XL 18), or a large pile of toadstools as refers to a3c6b23's
   plant ring effect. If these don't spawn, their locations swap
   in various other decorations: fountains, abandoned shops and trash,
   caches of food, or blood being mopped up into a bucket.

 * Pillar walls dotting each arena have a 40% chance of being
   demonic trees, a 40% chance of being crystal walls, a 15% chance of
   being thematic statues, and a 5% chance of being more of the permaglass
   surrounding the arena.

 * 33% of the time, there's two mixed consumables / single charges of
   wands and some off to the side from the exit. If the player doesn't
   pick these up but still wins the duel, it'll be deposited at their
   feet the same way monster drops are dumped out after clearing Okawaru's
   Duel. If they leave using an exit, they don't get any of such.

 * 40% of the time, there's some permanent teleport traps dotted in the
   arena to help frailer characters get some distance from the sudden
   enemy ambush, though there's not a lot of space in the arena in general
   to be escaping very far with.

 * Exits require opening three disconnected doors in a row, making it
   implausible to escape but far from impossible. Their locations are
   somewhat far from the start and are prerevealed alongside the rest of
   the map.

Some arena maps are far meaner than others in terms of exit accessibility,
clumping of incoming threats, or a safe chokepoint to stand in case of
summons. This is, of course, fully in the nature of Xom. We'll have to
see just how dangerous this effect works out in practice with all the
other buffs to Xom....

Xom bazaar update for chaotic talismans and unrands

 * With years having passed without any other god yet picking up direct
   Shapeshifting support, despite more and more talisman designs spreading
   their appeal beyond slot-limited unarmed combat, it is reasonable for
   the chaos god already providing some of the only god-gift talismans
   in the game to get a further nudge up there. Xom bazaars initially had
   three talismans before losing such in aa93178 due to the overbearing
   singular presences of granite and storm talismans for those who would
   care about shapeshifting, and the tripling of the talisman count since
   then makes it reasonable to bring a third talisman back: in true
   Xom fashion, this is always a chaotic randart talisman as set-up by
   9ee9fbd (which applies chaos to ~16.6% of all attacks). This commit
   also sets up some tiering structure for said talisman shop inventory,
   mostly to make the plain talisman always tier-3 or above, and to avoid
   the randart ones going for full-body tier 2 talismans as have major
   fall-off around and past the first Xom bazaar's depth.

 * As has been requested in the past, the chaotic-modified weapon unrands
   are now no longer handpicked, and can now pull anything that spawns
   randomly in a normal game (so, not the extended lord equipment or the
   Axe of Woe). To avoid this making the weapon picks bias heavily
   towards the weapon types with the most unrands (Maces & Flails plus
   polearms), this commit sets up some basic structuring to choose from
   all weapon types equally followed by any individual unrand choice.
   Sadly, this does make some of the previous extreme high-rolls fairly
   less common (like Rift or Gyre and Gymble), but should also introduce
   enough other unique rolls (like Fimbulwinter or Arga) at the same time.
   While I'm still a little worried that people will expect much fancier
   behaviour from this flag than is intended (with one-off effects like
   sundering or discharges or spell enhancing all getting chaotic brands),
   this should be reasonable enough for variety's sake as another step
   forward.

 * With the set-up of c738e17, this commit also adds a chance to roll
   chaotic body and aux armour unrands in the Xom bazaar (which have a
   low chance additionally scaled to damage taken to apply the chaos
   list of buffs and debuffs to the attacker), meant as another
   difficult purchasing decision point beyond the chaos weapons or
   talismans or narrowed spell support. Unlike the weapons being
   fairly uncontrolled in size or wielding applications, this also
   sets up some very basic species checks to avoid providing unwearable
   body armour 80% of the time, as the joke of being offered something
   completely unusable doesn't work if it's being done constantly,
   as well as to somewhat make up for how this is eating into other
   unrand chances:

   * Previously: 37.5% unmodified weird unrands, 37.5% chaotic weapon
     unrands, 25% no unrands.
   * Now: 30% unmodified weird unrands, 30% chaotic weapon unrands,
     20% chaotic armour unrands, 20% no unrands.

   The actual value of these unrands is shakier than the weapon unrands-
   without the brand damage, chaos can fairly easily roll its monster
   buffs- though the rarity of applying it alongside the chance of
   rolling something debilitating to the monster makes this probably
   better off than the still-perfectly-fine *Slow on equipment
   usually better off than the average randart.

In a similar vein to chaotic unrand weapons, chaotic armour gives a small

Fix a very rare issue with Xom banishment and level stack checking

Xom is not supposed to banish you if you're already in the Abyss.
is_level_on_stack() was used to check if the Abyss was somewhere 'above'
where you currently where, but it was effectively only checking Abyss:1.

This meant that it was technically possible, if you were on a deeper floor
of the Abyss and Xom sent you to a Bazaar, that they could then
subsequently banish you again while Abyss:4 (or whatever) was on the level
stack.

This is a very unlikely sequence of events, but it's better to be correct
(and this is less boilerplate, too).

Add exploration backbone to Xom, shift most strategic effects over to it

Historically, most Xom actions have been time-based, which for most of the
game's history allowed the player the theoretical ability to obtain an
unlimited number of good items and mutations by waiting around for a very
long time. Now, Xom would also do negative things to the player during that
time, of course, but there were increasingly popular strategies to minimize
negative effects while maximizing positive ones.

Several attempts were made in past to counter these strategies, and make
Xom harsher on the player specifically when it looked like they were
waiting around instead of playing normally. Unfortunately, much of this
either had limited impact or (far worse) made the act of playing Xom
'as intended' much more unpleasant (eg: Xom complaining or excessively
malmutating the player when clearing floors normally, or returning to an
earlier floor to shop).

This commit is the beginning of an attempt to address these issues on a
more fundamental level: *all* strategic/long-term benefits that Xom can
provide will now be metered by exploration, rather than time. Which is to
say that waiting around in place can never result in item gifts, mutations,
bazaar trips, or anything of that nature. This goes also for most long-term
*negative* effects, like draining or malmutation. Xom will continue to hand
out both gifts and punishments as the player explores, but there will be no
benefit to waiting around in place (and no penalty for shopping trips or in
general being slow).

The hope here is that this can put a final nail in the coffin of
Xomscumming without making it feel punative. It also allows some room to
create more interesting medium-term negative effects while having a modicum
of control over their frequency.

Subsequent commits will add numerous new explore effects - both positive
and negative.

Remove 'severity' as a parameter of Xom actions, replace with tension

With Xom mood removed, this was was effectively a completely random roll.
Severity was already ignored by most Xom effects entirely, but for those
which used it, it effectively just made their internal randomization
slightly harder to read.

In cases where it was used, I replaced it with something that felt vaguely
correct - sometimes the current average value, sometimes something higher
or lower or simpler. There will be small changes in the effectiveness of
various actions, but everything is in flux for the moment.

Tension is now what is passed to Xom actions. This is unused by almost all
of them, but it's there for any that care.

Carefully debone all gargoyles and djinn

This mostly affects flavour messages, with the single mechanical effect of
preventing them from having the Thin Skeletal Structure mutation (which, to
be fair, is also mostly for flavour).

But if the ants don't have a skeleton, it feels baffling that a stone
statue *would*.

Remove Xom boredom

Xom boredom worked by the player needing to keep Xom amused,
with punishment for failure to do so.

While flavourful, the details of this were somewhat troubled. The
details were opaque, and there were some trivial, renewable ways
to amuse Xom, like hitting yourself with a bouncing cast of Shock.

The importance of this system was largely to punish Xomscumming
by preventing waiting on nearly explored levels. A follow-up commit
will obviate this by moving Xom's strategic effects to an exploration
based system, removing the value of Xomscumming.

We continue to log messages when Xom finds something funny, and continue
to do so in the god channel - Xom has lots of other purely flavoursome
messages. We do this in proportion to their interestingness, replacing
a previous checked that only logged events which raised Xom's interest
in you.

Update all of Xom's notes to use severity

Piety is constant now. We log severity where it is actually used, and
otherwise -1.

Remove Xom mood

Xom's "mood" (a.k.a. piety) drifted randomly, affecting the chance
and severity of good and bad actions.

This had some bad incentives, encouraging mood "farming" for dangerous
fights and other situations (and after an upcoming change, would have
encouraged it for exploration). Even when these incentives were very
limited, they could feel important. It was also generally unclear to
players that Xom's mood was entirely unrelated to the things you did
which amused him.

Here, we rip the mood machinery out entirely. Xom now does not use
piety in any way. All effects that used piety for their severity now
sample a severity per-call, so subsequent calls are uncorrelated.

We repurpose the god-title pip bar as a tension meter, which is the
thing that still effects how nice Xom is.
